newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended firmer on Tuesday, although weaker U.S. treasuries pulled Europe off midsession highs, while short-dated Dutch paper continued to underperform, dealers said.
"There seem to be nerves about interest rate rises in the U.S., but we've had support from German fundamentals," one trader said.

Dutch bonds mirrored their German counterparts through the day, except for the short end. Shorter dated paper continued to suffer the effects of the Dutch central banks raising of special advances and secured loans rates on Monday.

The rate rise had little immediate impact on the mark/guilder rate which was unchanged on Tuesday. Some traders, however, said it should take effect soon, removing the need for further Dutch interest rate rises.

"With the rate hike, there is a difference of only 0.1 between the (Dutch special) advances and the German repo (rates) and Dutch fundamentals are better. The guilder will strengthen in coming weeks," one trader said.
Overall, business was slack with prices marked, not bought, higher. Traders said fellow players remained uncertain about U.S. interest rates and maintained a "wait-and-see" approach.
